01 / The operating model

Inspect the whole workflow.

The task is only one part of the system. Reliable automation also needs context before work, checks before use, clean handoffs, and a recovery owner when something breaks.

  1. 01

    Context

    What must the system know before work begins?

  2. 02

    Work

    What action actually changes the operating state?

  3. 03

    Checks

    How do we know the output is safe to use?

  4. 04

    Handoffs

    What context must survive between people and tools?

  5. 05

    Recovery

    Who owns the failure path when automation stops?

Recovery records what failed and feeds better context into the next run. It is part of the workflow, not cleanup after it.

02 / System choice

Agent, script, or process change?

I choose based on uncertainty, input stability, judgment, and failure cost—not because an agent sounds more impressive.

01

Agent

Use when the work needs bounded judgment across variable inputs.

02

Script

Use when inputs and outputs are stable enough to stay deterministic.

03

Process change

Use when the recurring problem is ownership, timing, or a missing decision rule.

03 / How the system behaves

Checks survive the handoff.

The interesting part is rarely the first successful run. It is what happens when context moves, a check fails, or a human needs to take over without reconstructing the whole story.

Checked handoff

Move the context with the work.

A handoff should preserve what happened, what was checked, what remains uncertain, and who owns the next decision.

Recovery loop

Failure becomes better input.

When automation stops, recovery should capture the missing context and improve the next run instead of hiding the failure.

05 / Start small

Bring one task that keeps coming back.

The first useful brief is not “add AI.” It is a concrete recurring task, the context it needs, how the result is checked, and what currently happens when it fails.

  1. Name the recurring task and its current owner.
  2. List the context required before work begins.
  3. Define the check that makes an output safe to use.
  4. Describe the handoff and the failure path.
